practiceQuestions.q: An NRI (Non-Resident Indian) is legally classified under which of the following acts for tax and residency purposes?
practiceQuestions.sol: An NRI is an Indian citizen who resides outside India for employment, business, or other purposes. Legally, the term is primarily defined under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999, alongside the Income Tax Act for tax purposes, but fundamentally an NRI holds an Indian passport.

practiceQuestions.q: In which year was the Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) scheme introduced by amending the Citizenship Act, 1955?
practiceQuestions.sol: The OCI scheme was introduced by amending the Citizenship Act, 1955 in 2003 (via the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003), following the recommendations of the High Level Committee on Indian Diaspora headed by L.M. Singhvi.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary distinguishing legal characteristic of an NRI compared to an OCI cardholder?
opts: NRI holds a foreign passport while OCI holds an Indian passport
NRI is an Indian citizen, whereas OCI is a foreign citizen holding a lifelong visa card
NRI has voting rights in Indian Lok Sabha elections, whereas OCI does not
NRI cannot own agricultural land in India, whereas OCI can
practiceQuestions.sol: An NRI is an Indian citizen living abroad and thus holds an Indian passport. An OCI is technically a foreign national of Indian origin who has been registered under Section 7A of the Citizenship Act, 1955.

practiceQuestions.q: The PIO (Person of Indian Origin) card scheme was formally merged with which status in January 2015?
practiceQuestions.sol: The PIO card scheme was withdrawn and merged with the OCI card scheme in January 2015 to create a single, unified diaspora cardholder category known as the OCI cardholder.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Article 9 of the Constitution of India, if a citizen of India voluntarily acquires citizenship of a foreign State, what happens to their Indian citizenship?
opts: It is retained as dual citizenship
It ceases to exist immediately (Single Citizenship principle)
It converts automatically into OCI status
It remains valid until the Indian passport expires
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 9 of the Indian Constitution clearly states that persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State shall not be citizens of India. India strictly follows the principle of single citizenship.

practiceQuestions.q: Which committee recommended the creation of the OCI category in India?
opts: High Level Committee on Indian Diaspora (L.M. Singhvi Committee)
practiceQuestions.sol: The High Level Committee on the Indian Diaspora, constituted in 2000 under the chairmanship of L.M. Singhvi, recommended the amendment to the Citizenship Act to grant dual nationality/OCI status to persons of Indian origin in certain countries.

practiceQuestions.q: Are OCI cardholders permitted to vote in Indian Parliamentary or State Legislative Assembly elections?
opts: Yes, if they reside in India for more than 182 days
No, OCI cardholders do not have voting rights in India
Yes, they can vote after registering with the Election Commission
Yes, but only in municipal and local body elections
practiceQuestions.sol: OCI cardholders are foreign nationals and do not possess voting rights in India, nor can they contest elections to Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, or Councils, and they cannot hold constitutional posts like President, Vice-President, or Judges.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 2010, voting rights were extended to which category of overseas Indians?
opts: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) who are Indian citizens
All Persons of Indian Origin holding foreign passports
practiceQuestions.sol: The Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 2010 enabled Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) who are citizens of India and have not acquired citizenship of any other country to register as voters in their constituency in India.

practiceQuestions.q: Can an OCI cardholder purchase agricultural land, farmhouses, or plantation property in India?
opts: No, OCI cardholders are barred from acquiring agricultural land, farmhouses, or plantation properties in India
Yes, with prior permission from the Supreme Court of India
Yes, if they inherit it from Indian relatives
practiceQuestions.sol: As per RBI and FEMA regulations, OCI cardholders cannot acquire agricultural land, farmhouses, or plantation property in India. However, they can acquire residential and commercial properties.

practiceQuestions.q: Which ministry serves as the nodal ministry dealing with matters relating to Overseas Indians, including NRIs and OCI cardholders?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) is the nodal ministry for matters relating to Overseas Indians. The erstwhile Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs (MOIA) was merged into the MEA in January 2016.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does India constitutionally and statutorily prohibit dual citizenship for Indian nationals, while offering OCI status to persons of foreign nationality with Indian roots?
opts: To maintain absolute allegiance to the nation, prevent divided loyalties, and preserve sovereign security, while keeping economic and cultural ties intact via OCI.
Because Article 5 of the Constitution explicitly bans all forms of international mobility.
To prevent foreign nationals from holding any employment within India.
To collect higher income taxes exclusively from NRIs without taxation for OCIs.
practiceQuestions.sol: India follows the single citizenship model (Article 9) to prevent divided political loyalties and ensure undivided allegiance. However, recognizing the diaspora's economic, financial, and emotional contribution, the OCI framework was created as a quasi-citizenship/lifelong visa vehicle without granting political rights.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the tax liability of an NRI differ significantly from that of an OCI cardholder living abroad?
opts: NRIs are taxed on their global income in India, whereas OCIs are never taxed in India.

NRIs are taxed in India only on their Indian-source income, but tax residency rules depend on physical presence under the Income Tax Act, whereas OCI tax status depends entirely on where they reside and earn, as they are foreign citizens.
OCI cardholders pay double income tax on all earnings worldwide compared to NRIs.
There is no difference; both are subjected to identical tax slabs under the Income Tax Act.
practiceQuestions.sol: An NRI is an Indian citizen, and their tax liability in India is determined by their residential status under the Income Tax Act (Resident, RNOR, or Non-Resident), taxing only Indian-source income if non-resident. An OCI is a foreign citizen; their tax liability in India applies strictly to income earned or accrued within India, similar to any foreign national.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the rationale behind merging the PIO card scheme with the OCI card scheme in 2015?
opts: To eliminate confusion caused by two parallel schemes providing overlapping benefits and to provide lifelong validity and hassle-free travel.
To strip foreign nationals of all economic privileges in India.
To convert all PIO cardholders into voting Indian citizens automatically.
To comply with United Nations mandates on diaspora management.
practiceQuestions.sol: The PIO card had a shorter validity (15 years) and required police reporting under certain conditions, whereas OCI offered lifelong multi-entry visas and exemption from registration. Merging them streamlined diaspora administration and eliminated administrative redundancy.

practiceQuestions.q: Consider the eligibility criteria for obtaining an OCI card: which category of individuals is strictly excluded from registration as an OCI cardholder?
opts: Individuals who have ever been citizens of Pakistan or Bangladesh.
Individuals who hold dual citizenship of the US and UK.
Individuals whose great-grandparents migrated from undivided India.
Individuals working in foreign multinational corporations.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Section 7A of the Citizenship Act, 1955, persons who are or have been citizens of Pakistan or Bangladesh, or whose child/grandchild/great-grandchild has been a citizen of Pakistan or Bangladesh, are explicitly barred from obtaining OCI status.

practiceQuestions.q: How do educational rights in India compare between an NRI student and an OCI cardholder student?
opts: NRIs are treated as domestic candidates for all seats, whereas OCI students are treated strictly as foreign nationals for all university admissions.
Both NRIs and OCIs are eligible for parity with domestic Indian citizens for admission to seats meant for Indian nationals, following Supreme Court rulings and statutory amendments.
OCI students have preferential access to reservation seats in public universities over resident Indian citizens.
NRIs cannot study in Indian professional institutions without prior diplomatic clearance.
practiceQuestions.sol: Following legal clarifications and Supreme Court judgments (such as the Modi-Entel case and subsequent notifications), OCI cardholders have been equated with Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) in the matter of all-India entrance tests like NEET, JEE, etc., making them eligible for admission against NRI/domestic seats rather than purely foreign quotas, subject to parity notifications.

practiceQuestions.q: In terms of professional practice in India (such as practicing medicine, law, architecture, or chartered accountancy), what are the legal boundaries for OCI cardholders compared to NRIs?
opts: NRIs face absolute prohibition, while OCIs have unlimited professional practice rights.

NRIs (being Indian citizens) enjoy full professional rights, whereas OCI cardholders may require specific statutory approvals or registrations with respective professional councils (like MCI/NMC, Bar Council) depending on prevailing statutory rules.
Neither NRIs nor OCIs can practice any profession in India.
OCIs are automatically granted Indian professional licenses without qualification checks.
practiceQuestions.sol: NRIs are Indian citizens holding Indian degrees or recognized foreign qualifications and retain full civic and professional rights. OCI cardholders can practice professions in India, but parity with Indian citizens in professional fields is subject to notifications by the Central Government, and certain regulated professions may require specific clearances.

practiceQuestions.q: Can an OCI cardholder be appointed to public employment under the State (Government jobs under Article 16)?
opts: Yes, to all central and state government civil services positions without exception.
No, unless specific notifications are issued by the Central Government opening particular posts/services to OCI cardholders.
Yes, automatically because OCI status confers quasi-citizenship rights.
Only in judicial and defense services.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment for citizens of India. Since OCI cardholders are foreign nationals, they are not automatically eligible for government jobs, but the Central Government specifies particular posts or services where OCI cardholders can be employed.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2021 empower the Central Government regarding OCI card cancellation?
opts: It allows cancellation only if the OCI holder commits a heinous crime punishable with capital punishment.
It empowers the government to cancel OCI registration for violation of any provision of the Citizenship Act or any other law in force, ensuring an opportunity of being heard is provided.
It automatically revokes all OCI cards after 10 years of issuance.
It transfers OCI cancellation powers exclusively to the Supreme Court of India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2021 added provisions enabling the cancellation of OCI registration if there is a violation of the Citizenship Act or any other central law, ensuring procedural fairness by mandating an opportunity to be heard.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the legal implication of holding an Indian passport for an NRI versus an OCI cardholder?
opts: Both hold Indian passports as proof of Indian nationality.
An NRI holds an Indian passport because they are an Indian citizen, whereas an OCI cardholder holds a foreign passport and is issued an OCI registration booklet/visa sticker.
An OCI cardholder holds a dual passport issued by the Ministry of External Affairs.
An NRI carries a foreign passport while working abroad.
practiceQuestions.sol: An NRI is an Indian citizen residing abroad and therefore must hold a valid Indian passport. An OCI cardholder is a citizen of a foreign country and travels on their foreign passport, supplemented by an OCI registration document/lifelong visa.

practiceQuestions.q: Which constitutional rights available under Part III of the Constitution of India are strictly denied to OCI cardholders while being fully available to NRIs?
opts: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty (Article 21)
Right to Freedom of Speech, Assembly, and Movement specifically reserved under Article 19 as citizen-only rights.
practiceQuestions.sol: Certain Fundamental Rights in Part III (Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30) are available exclusively to citizens of India. Since NRIs are Indian citizens, they enjoy these rights. OCI cardholders, being foreign nationals, do not enjoy citizen-only rights like Article 19 (freedom of speech, expression, movement, settlement, profession).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Non-Resident Indians (NRIs):
1. An NRI is defined under the Income Tax Act, 1961 and FEMA, 1999 as an Indian citizen who stays abroad for employment or business or under circumstances indicating an intention for an uncertain duration of stay.
2. NRIs enjoy all fundamental rights under the Indian Constitution, including the right to vote in Indian elections, subject to registration in electoral rolls.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. NRIs are Indian citizens; hence, they enjoy all fundamental rights available to citizens (unlike OCI cardholders who are foreign nationals). Following the RP (Amendment) Act, 2010, registered NRIs can vote in Indian parliamentary and assembly elections in their constituencies.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Overseas Citizens of India (OCI):
1. The OCI scheme was introduced by amending the Citizenship Act, 1955 in the year 2003.
2. An OCI cardholder is granted dual citizenship of India and the foreign country of their residence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: OCI was introduced via the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003. Statement 2 is incorrect because India does NOT permit dual citizenship. OCI is NOT dual citizenship; it is a lifelong multi-entry visa status/quasi-citizenship granted to foreign nationals of Indian origin.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following comparisons between NRI and OCI cardholder regarding economic and property rights:
1. Both NRIs and OCI cardholders can acquire residential and commercial properties in India.
2. OCI cardholders are permitted to acquire agricultural land and plantation property in India just like NRIs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Both NRIs and OCIs can purchase residential and commercial properties in India. Statement 2 is incorrect because OCI cardholders are strictly prohibited from acquiring agricultural land, farmhouses, or plantation property in India, whereas NRIs are permitted to inherit or purchase certain agricultural properties under specific FEMA guidelines.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the merger of PIO and OCI card schemes:
1. The Person of Indian Origin (PIO) card scheme was merged with the OCI card scheme in January 2015.
2. Existing PIO cardholders were required to convert their cards into OCI cards by specified deadlines, and the PIO scheme stands completely rescinded.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Government of India merged the PIO card scheme with the OCI scheme in January 2015, and all existing PIO cardholders were directed to obtain OCI cards to avail seamless lifelong travel and residency benefits.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding political and constitutional rights in India:
1. OCI cardholders can contest elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
2. NRIs are eligible to contest elections to the Parliament and State Legislatures provided they are registered electors in India and meet statutory age and qualification criteria.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because OCI cardholders are foreign nationals and do not possess voting or contesting rights in India. Statement 2 is correct because NRIs are Indian citizens; if they are registered voters and meet the qualifications under the Representation of the People Act, they can contest elections.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding visa and travel requirements for visiting India:
1. An NRI requires a valid Indian passport and does not require any visa to enter India.
2. An OCI cardholder requires a foreign passport along with an OCI registration certificate (lifelong multi-entry visa) to visit India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate. NRIs are Indian citizens travelling on Indian passports; hence, visa requirements do not apply. OCIs are foreign nationals holding foreign passports who possess a lifelong multi-entry OCI visa sticker/card to enter India without separate visa hassles.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding constitutional provisions on citizenship (Articles 5-11):
1. Article 9 of the Constitution explicitly states that if a person voluntarily acquires the citizenship of a foreign State, their Indian citizenship terminates automatically.
2. The Constitution of India lays down detailed provisions for the regulation of citizenship rights and OCI cardholders through permanent constitutional articles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct under Article 9. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Constitution under Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law (leading to the Citizenship Act, 1955). OCI status is statutory (created by the 2003 amendment), not constitutional.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding economic and financial transactions for NRIs and OCIs under FEMA:
1. Both NRIs and OCI cardholders can open and maintain Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) and Non-Resident External (NRE) bank accounts in India, subject to RBI regulations.
2. Repatriation of funds from India is permitted for both NRIs and OCI cardholders under specified limits and procedural guidelines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under FEMA regulations, both NRIs and OCI cardholders are permitted to operate NRE, NRO, and FCNR accounts, and can repatriate funds subject to compliance with RBI guidelines and applicable taxes.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the rights to public employment and higher education for OCI cardholders:
1. OCI cardholders have parity with Non-Resident Indian (NRI) citizens in respect of all-India entrance tests like NEET and JEE for university admissions.
2. OCI cardholders are automatically entitled to hold civil and military posts under the Union and State governments without any special government notification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Judicial rulings and notifications have placed OCI cardholders at par with NRIs for educational entrance exams like NEET/JEE. Statement 2 is incorrect because OCI cardholders are foreign nationals and cannot hold government employment unless specific posts are notified by the Central Government; they are strictly barred from constitutional and high public offices.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the termination or cancellation of OCI status:
1. The Central Government can cancel an OCI registration if the cardholder has shown disaffection towards the Constitution of India.
2. An OCI cardholder can voluntarily renounce their OCI status by making a declaration in the prescribed manner, which results in the minor children of such persons also losing their OCI status.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct under Section 7D and Section 7C of the Citizenship Act, 1955. The Central Government holds statutory powers to cancel OCI registration on grounds such as disaffection, fraud, or national security. Voluntary renunciation by a parent also affects minor children as stipulated in the Act.
